title: Probabilistic Thinking
coreMove: Hold several possible futures with weighted odds and act where the payoff and downside are asymmetric.
sourcePressure: The official support frames probabilistic thinking as estimating likelihoods rather than pretending to certainty, with Bayesian thinking, fat-tailed curves, and asymmetries as the supported terms.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says anything can happen, so all predictions are equally weak.

sourceAnchors.name: Bayesian thinking
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support specifically includes Bayesian thinking as part of probabilistic thinking
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Bayesian thinking gives you permission to change the weight as new evidence arrives instead of defending the first number.

sourceAnchors.name: Fat-tailed curves
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support specifically includes fat-tailed curves as part of probabilistic thinking
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A fat tail is the part of the curve that keeps rare events from staying polite.

sourceAnchors.name: Asymmetries
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen support specifically includes asymmetries as part of probabilistic thinking
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The odds matter, but the shape of the payoff can matter more.

counterintuition: certainty is impossible so decide randomly

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: an emergency manager deciding when to issue a voluntary evacuation
exampleSpecs.stakes: waiting for certainty could trap residents if winds shift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rebecca lays three wind scenarios on the map with rough odds and chooses the notice because the low-probability bad outcome is too costly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ash specks landing on a laminated evacuation map

exampleSpecs.audience: a pharmacy manager ordering a scarce antibiotic
exampleSpecs.stakes: overordering wastes supply, underordering leaves patients untreated
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Patrick updates his order after two new clinic alerts change the likelihood of a weekend surge
exampleSpecs.firstImage: orange prescription bottles clicking inside a locked drawer

exampleSpecs.audience: an orchard manager deciding whether to run frost fans overnight
exampleSpecs.stakes: fuel costs are high, but a hard frost could damage blossoms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Paula weighs forecast ranges against blossom loss and starts the fans because the downside is asymmetric
exampleSpecs.firstImage: white blossom petals trembling under a portable frost fan

exampleSpecs.audience: a finance lead considering a loan with a strict covenant
exampleSpecs.stakes: a likely growth plan may still fail under one plausible revenue miss
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Min writes three revenue cases and notices the medium-bad case triggers a covenant breach before the cash actually runs out
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a loan covenant highlighted beside three revenue cases

exampleSpecs.audience: a nonprofit director deciding whether to insure an outdoor fundraiser
exampleSpecs.stakes: a small premium may protect the year's scholarship budget
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Matteo compare the rain probability with the scholarship loss instead of treating thirty percent as small
exampleSpecs.firstImage: linen tablecloths stacked beside a rain-insurance quote

exampleSpecs.audience: a security lead deciding whether a small anomaly deserves escalation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rare intrusion path may cause serious damage if dismissed as noise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Soren updates the intrusion odds after a second log pattern appears and isolates the server before proof is complete
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two red log entries separated by a long quiet hour

skillTargets: update beliefs when new evidence arrives
recognize fat-tail risk without technical formulas

tryThisNowSpec: Write three possible outcomes for one decision, give each rough odds, then circle the outcome whose cost or upside is most asymmetric.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
